summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and opening a PR, followed by resolving CodeRabbit's GitHub review post-PR.
summary.outcome: Planning was partially completed: the researcher ran successfully (HIGH confidence), RESEARCH.md and VALIDATION.md were written and committed. The workflow was mid-execution at the Nyquist gate step before spawning the planner — execution, QA, and PR creation had not yet started.

repo: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is fully key-agnostic (takes raw key bytes, no owner/recipient distinction) — directly reusable for the shared-folder move without modification.
share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder path — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move.
adoptSharedFolderResult must only be called once for the source result; calling it for the dest result would corrupt the sharedFolderTree projection (dual-emit bug).
sdkCore.moveItem throws on name collision ('An item with this name already exists in destination') — no auto-rename logic needed in the handler.
@internal on ensureFolderLoaded is documentation-only, not enforced — safe to call directly from web code without adding a new public alias.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist in shared-folder-projection.ts needs moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree added (currently only lists the 7 Phase 48 methods).

File IPNS key for re-encryption must be sourced from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', NOT from FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped; recipients cannot decrypt it) — same pattern as updateSharedFileHandler.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is key-agnostic and reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case.
moveItem throws on destination name collision — collision policy is throw, no auto-rename.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist — must add moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree for Phase 49.

workflow: CodeRabbit CLI review (coderabbit review --agent) runs before PR creation; after the PR is created, CodeRabbit also posts a GitHub review which should be addressed via /resolve-pr-reviews.
The GSD plan-phase chain for this project is: researcher → Nyquist VALIDATION.md → pattern-mapper → gsd-planner (Opus) → gsd-plan-checker revision loop until clean.
AI-SPEC gate can false-positive on non-AI keywords (e.g., 'eval' appearing in e2e requirement text) — gate is non-blocking and can be skipped with rationale documented.
UI-SPEC can be skipped (--skip-ui) when a new component mirrors an existing, already-coded design; gsd:ui-review can validate retroactively during QA.
To prevent 1Password signer from wedging during long AFK automated runs, disable repo-local commit signing with git config --local commit.gpgsign false.

friction: Global commit.gpgsign=true would have caused 1Password signer prompts to wedge the entire automated pipeline during AFK execution — required manual local override before proceeding.
AI-SPEC keyword gate false-positived on 'eval' from a normal e2e requirement string, creating a spurious review step that had to be manually dismissed.
UI safety gate triggered (frontend indicators found) despite the new MoveDialog design being fully established in existing code and CONTEXT.md, requiring an explicit --skip-ui justification.
open_items: Execute phase 49 via gsd:execute-phase (wave-based, atomic commits) — not yet started.
Run /simplify on the phase 49 diff after execution.
Run security-review and security:review, with extra scrutiny on the crypto re-encryption path.

After PR creation: wait for CodeRabbit's GitHub review, then run /resolve-pr-reviews to address inline comments.

Re-enable commit signing (git config --local --unset commit.gpgsign) after the session — the branch will need a signed rebase or admin override before merge since the repo enforces signed commits on PRs.
